does.text: The per-frame entry point. It runs five steps in a fixed order: drop last frame's one-frame entities, turn queued requests into teleport entities, count down their timers, finish the ones whose timer ran out or whose spell failed, then fix collision on the moved characters. A scratch frame structure carries lists from one step to the next.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll named pseudo-code, Update at EoCServer.dll+0x11521B0: the call order RemoveOneFrameComponents, ProcessRequests, ProcessKeepAliveTimers, FinalizeFinishedTeleports, UpdateEntityCollisions was read.

does.text: Not a per-frame method: other code calls it to ask for a teleport. It logs the request (origin and target) and appends it to the system's pending list; the entity work happens in the next ProcessRequests. Callers in EoCServer.dll include at least two stats-functor executors (functions that log ExecuteStatsFunctor and hold attack position or target context), so requests come from spell or passive effects carrying a teleport functor; which spells is a guess from that.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0x1150010 read (log string, array append); callers EoCServer.dll+0x1646200, +0x162AE40, +0x162CA70, +0x119E410 found by decomp grep, and only their strings were looked at.

does.text: Walks the pending requests and checks each with ValidateRequestParams. A valid request becomes a new teleport entity (deferred command buffer) carrying StateComponent (the request's origin and target, 0x28 bytes) and KeepAliveComponent (a 4-byte value copied from the request: the timer that ProcessKeepAliveTimers counts down); when the request carries a valid spell entity handle the same entity also gets SpellComponent (that handle plus the spell's initial target). The entities the teleport moves are collected per entity, and a second loop then creates one separate new entity per collected entry carrying ExecuteRequestOneFrameComponent (logged 'creating Teleport request for (%s) to position (%s)'). An invalid request that has a valid spell handle goes to a failed list that FinalizeFinishedTeleports answers.
does.evidence: Review (Opus, 14 Nov): EoCServer.dll+0x1150840 searched and read around the adds: ValidateRequestParams true guards the CreateEntity; helper EoCServer.dll+0x114DC40 allocates the type at DAT_18226aaac = StateComponent, +0x114D800 DAT_18226aacc = KeepAliveComponent, +0x114D9E0 DAT_18226aaec = SpellComponent (guarded by the request's spell handle being valid), +0x114D3E0 DAT_18226ab0c = ExecuteRequestOneFrameComponent; type ids resolved through their registration functions (+0x1BDA20, +0x1BD810, +0x1BD8C0, +0x1BD760). All four are ComponentFrameStorageAllocRaw adds. Which entities are collected for the second loop (origin only, or target too, and the position-equality test that skips some) was only partly read.

does.text: Rejects a request when its origin or target entity is not alive or has no transform; the rejection is logged (dead source or target, missing transform). A request given as plain positions with no entity skips these tests.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0x1152AE0: the eight log strings, two early false returns, and the flag bytes at +0xc and +0x1c of the request.

does.text: Each frame subtracts the frame time from a float timer in every live teleport entity's KeepAlive data. When a timer reaches zero or below it logs 'Timer finished for Teleport entity' and adds the entity to the frame's finished list.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0x1150390: query over persistent alive entities, float subtraction of the GameTime delta, compare against zero, the log string.

does.text: For each entry the frame marked as a failed spell ('Sending Finish event for failed spell') it creates a fresh entity carrying FinishedEventOneFrameComponent. For each teleport whose timer ran out it does the same ('Destroying and sending Finish event for Teleport entity') and destroys the teleport entity. So a FinishedEvent entity appears once per teleport that ends or fails.
does.evidence: Review (Opus, 14 Nov): EoCServer.dll+0x114F620: both blocks call helper EoCServer.dll+0x114D5F0, an AllocRaw add of the type at DAT_182258ebc = FinishedEventOneFrameComponent (registration +0x17B810); DestroyEntity of the finished entity in the second block.

does.text: At the start of every frame it destroys the entities found by two queries, which is what makes the request and finished-event components live for one frame. Which two types the queries use is not visible (type ids sit in globals); taken to be ExecuteRequest and FinishedEvent from the names.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0x1151DF0: two query loops each ending in DestroyEntity.

does.text: Logs and switches collision off for entities while a teleport is under way and on again afterwards. The fields it writes (eoc::BoundComponent is the likely one) were not read.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll named pseudo-code of UpdateEntityCollisions: only the two log strings and the flag reads were looked at.
